subject: Prompt ownership & model exclusion — evidence and operational path
messages:
From: Clara Hsu <clara.hsu@medisys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medisys.com
Date: 2027-08-29T16:12:00Z
Subject: Prompt & output ownership; operational evidence request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the product demo last week. Before we move to legal/procurement, Medisys needs clarity on a few items related to LLM data use and operational evidence. Procurement has asked that we gather these items this week so they can complete the risk review (deal MED-8342). High level asks: 

- A contractual commitment that customer-provided prompts/interactions will not be used to improve or retrain models (explicitly: no model updates, derivative model training, or transfer to other customers).
- Confirmation of customer ownership of prompts and generated responses (we want explicit language that outputs/derivatives remain customer property).
- A subprocessor inventory (names, locations, processing purpose) and any planned near-term changes.
- An evidence pack showing: onshore KMS availability (EU), SFTP or API export path for tenant data, deletion/proof-of-delete workflow, and an example audit trace for a sample interaction.

We're also evaluating whether we need a private/dedicated deployment for regulatory reasons — can you confirm what evidence differs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? I attached our DPA questions doc so you can see the procurement checklist.

Can you get us a candidate response and evidence links by EOD Tuesday (2027-08-31)? If you need more time, tell us what you can deliver.

Thanks,
Clara Hsu
Lead Counsel, Privacy & Security
Medisys

Attachment: Medisys_DPA_Questions_v1.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Clara Hsu <clara.hsu@medisys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-29T21:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Prompt & output ownership; operational evidence request

Clara —

Appreciate the clear checklist and the timeline. Short answer: we can meet Medisys's core asks; below is a concise summary and what we'll deliver by EOD Tuesday.

What Redwood can commit to (contract + operational):
- Explicit model-exclusion clause we can propose that prevents use of tenant interactions for model updates or transfer to third parties. This will be a DPA addendum + a specific sentence in the service terms.
- Customer ownership of prompts and generated outputs: we can provide a clause that grants customers exclusive rights to outputs and prevents derivative licensing by Redwood.
- Subprocessor inventory: we'll provide a CSV with current subprocessors, their processing purpose, and residency.
- Evidence pack: sample audit trace (redacted), SFTP export walkthrough, proof-of-delete process, KMS residency options (EU onshore + BYOK options for Dedicated/Private).

Notes on deployment differences:
- Hosted: fastest onboarding; we can attest to non-training operational controls and provide attestations + audit traces. For cryptographic custody and legal exclusivity, Hosted uses shared hardware but with per-tenant logical separation.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools; supports customer-specific KMS bindings and stronger contractual isolation. Evidence includes tenant-dedicated keys and capacity isolation docs.
- Private: full control plane in customer VPC/on-prem — strongest from a residency/control standpoint; we can package operational runbooks for audits.

Deliverables we'll attach by Tue EOD (2027-08-31):
1) redwood_subprocessor_map.csv (current inventory)
2) redwood_ops_evidence_checklist.pdf (contains sample audit trace snippets and SFTP export steps)
3) proposed DPA addendum language (text) and a short summary of evidence differences by deployment model

Action for you: please confirm which specific data classes you consider "sensitive" for this engagement (PHI, special category PII, or both) and whether Medisys requires onshore-only processing for all stages. That will determine whether we recommend Dedicated or Private for the procurement team.

I'll loop in Marissa (customer success) for the runbook/evidence pack and Kim (security) for the subprocessor attestation.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Legal
Redwood Inference

From: Clara Hsu <clara.hsu@medisys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medisys.com
Date: 2027-08-30T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Prompt & output ownership; operational evidence request

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick reply and plan. A few clarifications from procurement/legal: 

- Data classes: Medisys will treat all interaction text that includes patient identifiers as PHI (so PHI applies). Procurement will flag any solution that cannot provide onshore processing for PHI.
- We need the contractual clause to be explicit about derivatives: "Redwood will not use, train on, or transfer Customer interaction data or derived outputs for model training or to improve models made available to other customers."
- For evidence, please include a CSV template with columns we can map to our vendor review form (subprocessor, country, processing purpose, contact, SOC/ISO status, data residency).

Procurement wants an initial materials packet before their review meeting Wednesday 2027-09-01 at 10:00 AM CET. If you can provide the two attachments (subprocessor CSV + evidence checklist) and a short paragraph of suggested DPA wording now, procurement can pre-seed their reviewers.

If it's easier, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow 2027-08-31; please propose 2 windows.

Clara

Deliverables included (attachments + links):

- redwood_ops_evidence_checklist.pdf (attached) — includes sample audit trace, SFTP export guide, proof-of-delete steps, and KMS residency options

Redwood shall maintain operational controls and provide documentary evidence of said controls upon Customer request."

Quick answers to your questions:

- Dedicated: offers tenant-bound KMS and stronger isolation; recommended if Medisys requires onshore KMS for PHI processing.
- Private: recommended when Medisys needs full control plane and air-gapped evidence for regulators.

Proposed 30-min call slots (CET):
- Tue 2027-08-31 09:00–09:30
- Tue 2027-08-31 14:30–15:00

If either works, Marissa will send a calendar invite and we can walk procurement through the evidence pack live.

Next steps for procurement: review attached CSV + checklist, confirm which deployment you prefer, and we will turn the suggested DPA wording into a redline for your legal team.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Legal
Redwood Inference
